verdict.rationale: Smithery's token-scoping docs show a real access-control primitive — service tokens can be scoped to specific connections/apps and even user metadata, limiting which tools a token can 'list and call' — which partially satisfies the allowlist/per-tool control theme. Namespaces further support workspace-level API key scoping. However, there is no documented UI/API for platform engineers to explicitly allowlist or deny individual tools within a server (only connection/app-level scoping is shown), and no independent verification of enforcement. Missing for 10: explicit per-tool allow/deny list configuration, documentation on blocking specific tools within an otherwise-permitted server, and independent/hands-on confirmation that scoping is enforced as described.
